newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher as rate-sensitives jump.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher as rate-sensitives jump.

text.p: Shares in Stockholm showed irregular development on Wednesday, with rate-sensitives moving strongly ahead as bond yields tumbled but export companies losing out early on due to a stronger crown.

The all-share index rose 0.27 percent to 2,045.41 in turnover of 3.28 billion crowns, but the fortunes of the various sector indices varied widely. The bank index climbed 2.55 percent, whilst the forestry index fell 0.77 percent.
All of the banks made strong gains with the exception of S-E-Banken, but here a price fall was because the share was trading without rights to shares in property unit Diligentia.

"The financial market is facing a restructuring. It's not just speculation about Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken, it has to do with Nordbanken, Stadshypotek, Sparbanken and Foreningsbanken as well," one broker said.
Shares in Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken rose earlier this week on a report the two were in talks over a potential merger.
Export shares during the morning fell due to a stronger crown. Ericsson edged down 0.50 crown to 166 and the drugs sector index lost 0.62 percent. Volvo rose two crowns to 147.
